plain.text: It was decided that Paul would sail for Italy. Paul and other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who treated Paul kindly. They sailed slowly against the wind. At Fair Havens on Crete, it was late in the season and sailing was dangerous. Paul warned, "Our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also." But the centurion followed the pilot and the ship's owner, and the majority decided to sail on to spend the winter in a better harbour.

When a gentle south wind began to blow, they set sail. But soon a wind of hurricane force swept down. The ship was caught and driven along. They threw cargo and the ship's tackle overboard. For many days neither sun nor stars appeared, and they finally gave up all hope of being saved. Paul stood up and said, "Keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed. Last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me and said, 'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.' So keep up your courage, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me. Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island."

On the fourteenth night, the sailors sensed land. Fearing rocks, they dropped anchors. Some sailors tried to escape in the lifeboat, but Paul told the centurion, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved," so the soldiers cut the lifeboat loose. Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat: "Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head." He took some bread, gave thanks to God in front of them all, broke it and began to eat. They were all encouraged and ate. There were 276 people on board. At daylight they saw a bay with a beach. The ship struck a sandbar and the stern was broken to pieces by the waves. The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent escape, but the centurion wanted to spare Paul's life and stopped them. He ordered those who could swim to jump first, and the rest to follow on planks. In this way everyone reached land safely.

summary.bigIdea: In a terrible storm, Paul trusts God's promise, encourages everyone, and all 276 people reach land safely.
points: Paul warns against sailing, but the decision-makers ignore him.
In the storm, an angel promises Paul that everyone will survive.
Paul gives thanks for bread in front of everyone; the ship is wrecked but all are saved.
summary.reflection: Paul said, "I believe God that it will happen just as He told me." What promise of God could you hold on to in your storm?
